body_html:
How to think about it

  • Count money from the biggest note: ₹200 + ₹100 + ₹50 + ₹20 = ₹370.
  • Total cost: add the prices. Change: subtract the cost from what you pay.

Examples

Example

A clay pot costs ₹135. You pay ₹200.

₹200 − ₹135

Answer: ₹65 change

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the change to the priceChange is what is left: subtract.
Counting notes as 1 eachCount the value written on each note.

What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 270 + 10 = 280. Only the tens digit goes up.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 less. 410 − 10 = 400. 409 is only 1 less.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 more. 450 + 50 = 500. Counting by 50s, the numbers end in 00 or 50.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more. 463 + 100 = 563. Only the hundreds digit goes up.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 more. 175 + 25 = 200. Counting by 25s, the numbers end in 00, 25, 50 or 75.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 less. 800 − 50 = 750. 700 skips a number.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 less. 250 − 25 = 225. The numbers go down by 25 each time.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 150 and add 150 each time
Start at 150 and add 50 each time
Start at 50 and add 50 each time
Start at 150 and add 5 each time
items.e: 150 + 50 = 200, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 150 and add 50 each time.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 25 and add 25 each time
Start at 50 and add 50 each time
Start at 50 and add 25 each time
Start at 50 and subtract 25 each time
items.e: 50 + 25 = 75, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 50 and add 25 each time. 50 is the start, not the jump.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 695 + 5 = 700. 695 + 5 crosses the hundred to 700.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. Each figure has 2 more tiles. 5 + 2 = 7 tiles in Figure 4.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many dots are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 5, 10, 15. Each figure has 5 more dots. 15 + 5 = 20 dots in Figure 4. 16 counts on 1, not 5.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure has 2 more sticks. 7 + 2 = 9 sticks in Figure 4. Count the sticks, not the triangles.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 12, 10, 8. Each figure has 2 fewer tiles. 8 − 2 = 6 tiles in Figure 4. This pattern is shrinking.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many cubes are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 6, 9, 12. Each figure has 3 more cubes. 12 + 3 = 15 cubes in Figure 4.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure has 2 more chairs. 8 + 2 = 10 chairs in Figure 4. 16 counts 4 chairs for every table, but no chairs fit where tables touch.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of tiles?
c: Start at 1 and add 3 each time
Start at 1 and add 2 each time
Start at 1 and add 1 each time
Start at 2 and add 2 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 1 tile. Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. The pattern rule is start at 1 and add 2 each time.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of tiles?
c: Start at 12 and add 2 each time
Start at 12 and subtract 1 each time
Start at 12 and subtract 2 each time
Start at 8 and add 2 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 12 tiles. Count each figure: 12, 10, 8. The pattern rule is start at 12 and subtract 2 each time. The pattern gets smaller, so the rule subtracts.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of sticks?
c: Start at 4 and add 4 each time
Start at 4 and add 3 each time
Start at 3 and add 4 each time
Start at 1 and add 3 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 4 sticks. Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. The pattern rule is start at 4 and add 3 each time. 4 is how many sticks Figure 1 has. It is not the jump.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of cubes?
c: Start at 1 and add 3 each time
Start at 6 and add 6 each time
Start at 3 and add 3 each time
Start at 6 and add 3 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 6 cubes. Count each figure: 6, 9, 12. The pattern rule is start at 6 and add 3 each time. Each new tower has 3 cubes.

items.q: What does the scale on this column graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 1, 2, 3 … Each line is 1 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 1s.

items.q: Which column shows the most birds?
items.e: The column for Kookaburra is the tallest one. The column for Kookaburra ends on the line for 8. It shows 8 birds.

items.q: How many votes did Mango get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 1s. The column for Mango ends on the line for 6. So the answer is 6 votes.

items.q: Which column shows 3 students?
items.e: The scale goes up in 1s. Find 3 on the scale. The column for Cricket ends on the line for 3.

items.q: How many more books did Neha read than Nikhil?
items.e: The scale goes up in 1s. Neha: 7. Nikhil: 3. How many more means find the difference: 7 − 3 = 4 books.

items.q: What does the scale on this column graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many students have a cat?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Cat ends on the line for 10. So the answer is 10 students.

items.q: How many shells did Karan find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Karan ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 shells.

items.q: How many ice blocks were sold on Tuesday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Tue ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 ice blocks.

items.q: Which column shows 13 students?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 13 on the scale. The column for Dog ends halfway between 12 and 14, so it shows 13.

items.q: Favourite colour (frequency table): Red 5, Blue 8, Pink 3, Grey 6. Which column graph shows the same data?
items.e: C matches every number (the scale goes up in 1s). A: two columns are the wrong way round; B: one column is one line too high; D: one column is one line too low.

items.q: People in families (frequency table): 2 people: 4, 3 people: 9, 4 people: 12, 5 people: 7. Which column graph shows the same data?
items.e: A matches every number (the scale goes up in 2s). B: two columns are the wrong way round; C: a column is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); D: one column is one line too high.

items.q: Cans collected (frequency table): 3A 25, 3B 40, 3C 15, 3D 30. Which column graph shows the same data?
items.e: D matches every number (the scale goes up in 5s). A: two columns are the wrong way round; B: one column is one line too high; C: one column is one line too low.

items.q: Ice blocks sold (frequency table): Mon 11, Tue 6, Wed 14, Thu 9. Which column graph shows the same data?
items.e: B matches every number (the scale goes up in 2s). A: two columns are the wrong way round; C: a column is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); D: one column is one line too high.
First count the tallies: Dog 6, Cat 4, Fish 3, Bird 5. B matches every number (each symbol = 1). A: two rows are the wrong way round; C: one row has a symbol too many; D: one row is missing a symbol.
D matches every number (each symbol = 2). A: two rows are the wrong way round; B: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; C: one row has a symbol too many.
A matches every number (each symbol = 5). B: two rows are the wrong way round; C: one row has a symbol too many; D: one row is missing a symbol.

First count the tallies: Apple 10, Kiwi 7, Plum 12, Pear 5. C matches every number (each symbol = 2). A: two rows are the wrong way round; B: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Which list of numbers matches this column graph? The numbers are in this order: magpies, galahs, lorikeets, ibises.
items.e: The scale goes up in 1s. The column for Magpie ends on the line for 6. The column for Galah ends on the line for 9. The column for Lorikeet ends on the line for 4. The column for Ibis ends on the line for 7. Read the line at the top of each column, not the space above it.

items.q: The pictograph and the column graph show the same data. How many votes should the missing Banana column show?
items.e: Read the Banana row of the pictograph. Each circle = 2 votes. The Banana row has 4 circles and half a circle: 4 × 2 = 8, and half of 2 is 1, so 8 + 1 = 9 votes. Draw the Banana column up to 9.
